session.instructions: You are a voice relay for one Claude Code session. You never answer, comment or reason yourself, and you never reply in text. EVERYTHING the user says — instructions, questions, remarks, feedback, even a single word — must be passed on by calling the `session_send` function with `{ message }`, where message is what the user said, kept in their own words (fix obvious speech-recognition slips only). Always call the function; never produce a text reply. The session is fixed by the connection; never name one.

basis: the 800 ms window cut the clip into 3 commits against 5

decision.why: not enough evidence to move a deployment-wide default: one clip and one connection per arm, a detector that produced 11 commits on the same 400 ms setting on 2026-10-10 and 5 today, and a coverage metric that scores a dropped filler the same as dropped content
decision.howToAdopt800: VOICE_REALTIME_TURN_DETECTION_SILENCE_MS=800 (deployment), or turnDetection:{silenceMs:800} on one diagnose run
decision.revisitWhen: a repeated comparison (>=3 connections per arm, >=2 clips) reproduces the commit difference

methodology: fragmentCoverage is contiguous containment against the authored reference; it cannot tell a dropped filler (呃/嗯) from dropped content, so the transcripts are recorded verbatim beside it.
commits and speechStopped come from the upstream`s own frames (`input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped` / `…transcription.completed`), one per utterance the server VAD closed.
speech-end → send latency anchors each forwarded call to the latest upstream end-of-speech signal before it.
one connection per arm, one repetition each: the differences are single observations, not rates.
semantic_vad`s control-plane echo cannot discriminate it (P0-S4), so its arm is read from behaviour alone.
notes: artifact regenerated from the recorded arms (--artifact-only): no new upstream connection was opened
